newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Tutu says ANC amnesty issue resolved.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu says ANC amnesty issue resolved.

text.p: Archbishop Desmond Tutu said on Sunday a crisis threatening South Africa's truth commission had been averted after the ruling African National Congress denied claiming the right to absolve itself of human rights abuses.

Tutu, who threatened last week to quit as chairman of the commission, held nearly three hours of talks with ANC deputy secretary-general Cheryl Carolus and other ANC leaders on Sunday to clear the air.
"The perception was that you (the ANC) were granting yourselves amnesty," Tutu said in a joint news conference with Carolus afterwards.

"We were very, very concerned about that. If it had gone unchallenged, it would have...impugned the integrity of the commission and given the impression that it was being manipulated by the ANC," Tutu said.

Tutu issued his threat to resign after several senior ANC members appeared to signal that the movement felt it had committed no abuses during the struggle against apartheid for which it should seek amnesty.
Carolus told the news conference that the party believed the anti-apartheid struggle had been a just war but accepted that some members needed to go through the legal process of seeking amnesty.
She said this had always been the party's position, but misinterprations had arisen.
Tutu said the meeting had eased the commission's fears: "I think that we are satisfied."
President Nelson Mandela set up the commission last year with a mandate to form as full a picture as possible of abuses during the apartheid war.
Tutu hopes the commission, which has heard harrowing testimony from victims of police torture and from some of the torturers themselves, will help to heal the wounds of South Africa's past.
